questions.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3,$ then what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & -9 & -9 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 9{x}_{1}-9{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 9 & -9 & -9 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-9){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & -27 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=(-\frac{1}{9}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{3}.$ From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{-3}{1}=-3.$
